consensus_summary: Blind responses converge on lamp oil primarily symbolizing the Holy Spirit (anointing, inward presence, power, and sustaining light), especially via Zechariah 4, anointing texts, and popular readings of Matthew 25; common alternatives include readiness/watchfulness, good works, or faith/grace, with no fully settled scholarly consensus.
book_summary: Spirit-taught truth and correction received, kept, and worked into proven obedience—the tested, pressed fruit of the Spirit stored inwardly—with light as that obedience made visible as example to others.
rationale: The book explicitly notes the common Holy-Spirit reading and remains compatible with it (and with good-works/faith alternatives), yet materially sharpens and narrows the symbol to the inward storage of Spirit-produced, tested truth/correction/obedience rather than the Spirit per se or generic readiness; this is a precise, supported refinement rather than a match, displacement, or unrepresented novelty.
strongest_objection: The synthesis equates oil more with the fruit/obedience produced by the Spirit (and with reproof/truth) than with the Spirit Himself, potentially shifting weight toward a works-oriented alternative already present in the consensus while over-reading the 'pressed' metaphor and non-transferability.
